summary: This lecture tells the period after the first revelation until the revelation paused. The ustaz recalls Khadijah and Waraqah, who died soon after, then the Prophet SAW saw Jibril with six hundred wings and ran home asking to be covered, and Surah Al-Muzzammil came down commanding night prayer. Jibril taught wudu and the two daily prayers, and a few early believers joined, including Ali, Zaid, Abu Bakr, Abdurrahman ibn Auf, Uthman and Sa'd. When revelation paused he grew sad until Surah Ad-Duha came down to comfort him: Allah had not abandoned him, the Hereafter is better, He sheltered him as an orphan, guided and enriched him, then taught to care for orphans, not rebuke beggars and to proclaim the Lord's blessings. After three years of quiet calling, Allah would command open preaching.
keyPoints: The Prophet SAW saw Jibril with six hundred wings filling the sky and ran home asking to be covered.
Surah Al-Muzzammil commanded him to rise for night prayer, and Jibril taught wudu and the two prayers.
Revelation paused for some time until he grew sad and worried that Allah had abandoned him.
Surah Ad-Duha comforted him: Allah had not abandoned or hated him, and the Hereafter is better.
Allah taught not to rebuke the orphan, not to drive away the beggar and to proclaim the Lord's blessings.

chapters.title: Opening and recap
chapters.summary: The ustaz continues the class and recalls the first revelation and the Prophet running home.

chapters.title: Khadijah, Waraqah and An-Namus
chapters.summary: Khadijah took him to the elderly, blind Waraqah, who said it was the Namus that came to Prophet Musa.

chapters.title: Jibril with six hundred wings
chapters.summary: Waraqah died. Then in the desert he saw Jibril as large as the sky with six hundred wings, fell and ran home.

chapters.title: Surah Al-Muzzammil
chapters.summary: He asked to be covered and Allah revealed surah 73, calling him O you who are wrapped and telling him to rise for night prayer.

chapters.title: Wudu and the two prayers
chapters.summary: Jibril taught wudu and prayer, at first two times, before sunrise and sunset.

chapters.title: Revelation pauses
chapters.summary: After some time revelation stopped and he was anxious because Waraqah was gone and he had no one to ask.

chapters.title: The earliest believers
chapters.summary: Ali saw him pray with Khadijah, and the adopted Zaid ibn Harithah also believed.

chapters.title: Zaid and Abu Bakr
chapters.summary: The ustaz repeats Zaid's story, then Abu Bakr bravely became the first friend to follow and brought Abdurrahman, Uthman and Sa'd to Islam.

chapters.title: He grows sad
chapters.summary: Revelation was cut off for so long that he worried Jibril did not like him.

chapters.title: Surah Ad-Duha
chapters.summary: Jibril returned with Surah Ad-Duha, which means the soft morning light.

chapters.title: By the morning light and the night
chapters.summary: Allah swears by the bright morning and the silent night to soothe a sad heart.

chapters.title: Allah has not abandoned him
chapters.summary: Allah affirmed He had not abandoned or hated him, and that the Hereafter is better than this world.

chapters.title: Orphan, guidance and sufficiency
chapters.summary: Allah reminded him he was sheltered as an orphan, guided when searching and made self-sufficient.

chapters.title: Do not rebuke the orphan or beggar
chapters.summary: Allah commands not to rebuke the orphan or drive away the beggar, and to give kindly.

chapters.title: Proclaim your Lord's blessings
chapters.summary: The blessings of knowledge and the Quran should be shared, and the ustaz tells of a doctor who became the answer to a mother's prayer.

chapters.title: Three years of quiet calling
chapters.summary: He called quietly from age 40 to 43 before being commanded to preach openly.

sirah.summary: This lecture covers Surah Al-Muzzammil, the two prayers, the pause in revelation, Surah Ad-Duha and the start of quiet calling.

lessons.title: Allah does not abandon His servant
lessons.body: Even when we are sad, Allah does not abandon or hate us.

lessons.title: The Hereafter is better than this world
lessons.body: What awaits is better, including for those tested in this world.

lessons.title: Paradise never becomes dull
lessons.body: The pleasures of paradise grow ever better and never become dull like toys on earth.

lessons.title: Remember Allah's past favours
lessons.body: Allah reminded him: did I not find you an orphan and shelter you, lost and guide you.

lessons.title: The Quran is guidance
lessons.body: When we have a problem we open the Quran to find answers.

lessons.title: Do not oppress the orphan
lessons.body: Orphans should be cared for and comforted, not scolded or troubled.

lessons.title: Do not drive away beggars
lessons.body: Give kindly and do not demean the one who asks.

lessons.title: Spreading Allah's blessings
lessons.body: The blessing of knowledge and Islam should be shared with others.

lessons.title: Allah chooses us as an answer to prayer
lessons.body: The doctor's story shows Allah can make us a means of answering another's prayer.

lessons.title: Teaching those with fewer resources
lessons.body: Children who can read may teach poor neighbours to read the Arabic alphabet.
